model.name: Folders are drop targets — dropping content onto a folder places it inside that folder
model.description: Tron INTENT (capability, does NOT exist today): folders SHOULD BE drop targets; dropping content onto a folder places it INSIDE that folder. Currently folders are NOT drop targets (Tron dropped on the drop area, not a folder — see R40.85 regression). Frame as the BEHAVIOUR (folders accept drops + the dropped content lands in that folder), NOT merely fix-the-upload. Same CONTAINMENT theme as R40.83 (room-folder identity) + R40.84 (in-place add). User terms: when I drop content onto a folder, it lands inside that folder.

discoverySource.framing: CAPABILITY Tron wants (does not exist today), NOT a defect; PO split it from the R40.85 upload regression.

model.buildable: capability (new) — builds ON the fixed drop-area upload (R40.85); same room-folder containment surface.
model.crossRefNote: Containment family: R40.83 (resolve the destination folder by ONE identity), R40.84 (in-place tree update on the drop-add), R40.85 (the fixed upload path this builds on), R40.78 (add-folder-in-room containment). Ties the unit-IS-the-MVC-model + drop-resolves-destination-by-one-identity lessons.
model.satisfactionStatus: PARTIAL / RE-OPENED 2026-09-06. The ROOM-folder file-drop is GREEN (tester 6933f7c97 DET 3/3 v0.8.185: lands inside, renders as child, one unit, no regression). BUT the requirement is now BROADER after the scope correction: Folder-implements-DropTarget on EVERY surface (incl model) + the model-folder blob-create path = required work, architect redesigning. So R40.86 is NOT fully satisfied — the per-surface carve-out that would have called it done was struck. Honest partial per R40.54.

gateRef.assertion: a folder is a drop target (accepts + shows affordance); non-target => RED

acceptanceCriteria.text: Tron: dropping content onto a folder places it INSIDE that folder. Dropped content lands in the TARGET folder (containment), NOT at root or elsewhere. User terms: when I drop content onto a folder, it lands inside that folder.

gateRef.assertion: dropped content is contained in the target folder; landing at root/elsewhere => RED

acceptanceCriteria.stubMustFail: PENDING: seed a drop landing outside the target -> RED

acceptanceCriteria.text: The drop resolves the DESTINATION folder by the ONE canonical roomcoll identity (R40.83 lesson) — NOT a second/dual identity for the drop target. A wrong-destination from a divergent identity resolution => RED.

gateRef.assertion: the drop target resolves via the one roomcoll identity (RoomFolder); a dual/second-identity resolution => RED

acceptanceCriteria.stubMustFail: PENDING: seed a dual-identity drop-target resolution -> wrong dest -> RED

acceptanceCriteria.text: The drop-add updates the target node IN PLACE (R40.84): the tree does not collapse or rebuild wholesale, expanded state survives, only the target folder gains the child.

gateRef.assertion: drop-into-folder updates that node in place; full-tree collapse/rebuild => RED

gateRef.assertion: WE verify drop-into-folder containment before Tron sees it; Tron accepts

acceptanceCriteria.text: REVOKED 2026-09-06 (struck-in-place, NOT appended — the carve-out must not survive as text a future agent could act on). This AC WRONGLY enshrined a PER-SURFACE CARVE-OUT (room-folder file-drop IN / model-collection OUT) as a design BOUNDARY. It was a MISSING IMPLEMENTATION dressed up as scope. TRON OVERRULED (verbatim): 'a folder being a drop target is for every folder everywhere... not just in certain rooms. oop folder implements dropTarget... are you kidding me?' A Folder is a drop target EVERYWHERE by virtue of being a Folder; 'the model store has no blob-create path' is WORK TO BUILD, not a permitted absence. SUPERSEDED BY AC-folder-implements-droptarget + AC-model-blob-create-path-required. (WHY it changed: PO ratified a carve-out at my direction; Tron overruled; the capability belongs to the CLASS, not the rendering context.)

gateRef.assertion: struck; the drop-target capability is on the Folder CLASS (see superseding ACs), not a per-surface boundary

acceptanceCriteria.text: Every Folder IS a DropTarget — CLASS-KEYED, offered on EVERY folder surface with NO per-surface gate; no folder answers false to 'are you a drop target'. A drop into a MODEL-COLLECTION folder mints a File unit in MODEL_STORE UNDER it + renders INSIDE it + PERSISTS across reload. The capability belongs to the Folder CLASS, not the rendering/surface context (OOP-first, R40.82 sibling — a per-surface carve-out IS the functional-construct defect). UC generalises to folder.acceptDrop (the DropTarget contract).

gateRef.assertion: every folder surface offers drop (class-keyed, no per-surface gate) AND a model-collection-folder drop mints a File unit in MODEL_STORE under it + renders inside + persists

acceptanceCriteria.stubMustFail: DUAL stub-must-fail: (a) a SURFACE CARVE-OUT (a folder that is a drop target on one surface but not another) -> RED; (b) a model-folder drop that mints NOTHING (no File unit in MODEL_STORE) -> RED. A suite green on either => inadmissible.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The model store currently has NO create path for a dropped file/blob inside a model folder. This is a REQUIRED CAPABILITY TO BUILD (work owed), NOT a permitted absence or exclusion: a file dropped into a model folder MUST LAND (the create path is built so the drop has somewhere to go). Recorded as required work, never as a scope boundary.

gateRef.assertion: a file dropped into a model folder lands (create path exists); no-create-path => RED (work owed, not a boundary)

acceptanceCriteria.stubMustFail: PENDING: drop a file into a model folder -> currently nowhere to land -> RED until the create path is built
